title: Unique art style choices for my game?
author: Cautious-Western1298
selftext:
Hey guys! Im making a small AI-coded digital board game called **It’s Just Logic**. basically, it is a grid style 1v1 strategy game with hidden resources, territory expansion, and shop items, kind of like Battleship mixed with a tactical board game. I’m trying to decide between two UI styles. One is a really simple geometry style, mostly words, simple colors, and basic shapes. This would be way easier for me to make, and honestly I don’t think it would look that bad if I keep it consistent. The other option is more of a command-room / battle-map style, like a tactical screen where Im planning moves, like what you see in some military movies. That one probably fits the game better and would look cooler, but it would also be harder for me to make and polish. I’m not saying AI-made stuff is bad, cuz AI helped me with the code, and that’s fine, I just think the game would be better if it also had my own style and direction, so people won’t just go in and say it’s slop and no human effort. I also really enjoy creating my own style, so which one should I go with? And I will very appreciate more tips and comments :D 

thanks!

comments.author: Dry-Pickle-6121
comments.body:
okay, so here is how I would approach this issue. Sign up for one month of Mid-Journey, use the "Draft" feature, and stamp out your ideas for concept art. Like create a lot of different pieces of art and slowly start narrowing down what you find enjoyable. (Don't make videos, videos = expensive). 

Mid-Journey's draft feature is perfect for this though, as once you establish the Mood you are going for, you can leverage that into creating a balanced UI that matches your vision. 

Just my 2c.
